title: Game Director renders a failed load as "no sessions" and drops the error
body:
## Summary
useGameDirector maps every failed read to an empty list / null and never returns useCRUD's error, so a down /api/game-director looks like a project with no playtests.

## Description
src/hooks/useGameDirector.ts:41-52 fetchDirectorData turns each failed tryApiFetch into `[]`/`null` and never throws, so useCRUD (src/hooks/useCRUD.ts:72-74) never sets `error`; src/hooks/useGameDirector.ts:85 also discards `error` from the useCRUD result and the result type (:54-82) has no error field. The pair in the same context refuses this: src/hooks/useImplementationPlan.ts:218-220 ("A failed load must not be rendered as no features anywhere") and src/hooks/useModuleAggregates.ts:39-42 expose `failed`/`error`. Fixed = fetchDirectorData throws when the sessions read fails (keeping partial stats/trend when only those fail is a choice), useGameDirector returns `error` + `retry`, and src/components/modules/game-director/GameDirectorModule.tsx renders it (another context's file, hence B).

## Flow
- /api/game-director?action=list returns 500
- fetchDirectorData resolves {sessions:[]}
- GameDirectorModule shows the empty state, no error, no retry

## Expected impact
Operators stop reading an outage as "no playtests recorded". Could break: a view that relies on sessions staying [] on error.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed load is shown as a failure
Before: 3 of 3 reads map failure to empty; error exposed: 0 (read src/hooks/useGameDirector.ts:47-51,85)
After: predicted: hook test with list read failing -> result.error non-null; module renders an error banner
Method: simulation - the UI half lives in another context, so the gate could not be built here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook(useGameDirector) with tryApiFetch(list) -> {ok:false}; assert result.error set; GameDirectorModule test asserts the error text renders

title: NBA run evidence mixes every project: session_analytics carries no project
body:
## Summary
recordSessionOutcome posts no project and the run-evidence reads are unscoped, so the NBA success odds for a module count runs from every project ever opened.

## Description
src/hooks/useSessionAnalytics.ts:212-235 posts moduleId/sessionKey/prompt but no projectPath; src/hooks/useModuleRunEvidence.ts:81-82 and :110-111 read `?action=module` / `?action=dashboard` with no project, and its caches are process-wide, not project-keyed. The pair in the same context does the opposite: src/hooks/useModuleAggregates.ts:65-67 and :103-106 key every entry by project ("serving it would show one project's roll-up under another's name"). The spend-attribution technique (software-engineering/cost-metering) names the axes to capture at write time; project is the tenant axis here and history before it must report as "before attribution began", not be backfilled. Fixed = nullable project column on session_analytics (additive migration), recordSessionOutcome sends useProjectStore projectPath, the route filters by it, run-evidence caches key by project.

## Flow
- open project A, run 10 failing arpg-combat checklists
- switch to project B
- NBA card for arpg-combat scores B's odds from A's 10 failures

## Expected impact
NBA odds and the Unified Summary Activity dimension describe the open project only. Could break: dashboards that expect global totals (keep an unscoped view).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - run evidence describes the open project
Before: project axis on the write: 0 of 1 recorder; scoped reads: 0 of 2 (src/hooks/useModuleRunEvidence.ts:81,110)
After: predicted: route test seeding rows for two projects returns only the queried project's count
Method: simulation - needs a migration and route change outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: session-analytics route test: insert rows for projects A and B, GET ?action=module&projectId=A returns A only; hook test that a project switch re-reads

title: execute() dispatches without project context while a scan is already running
body:
## Summary
useModuleCLI.execute awaits scanProject, but scanProject returns at once when a scan is in flight, so the prompt is composed without the dynamic context the scan is about to produce.

## Description
src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:228-229 `await scanProject()`; src/stores/projectStore.ts:120 returns immediately when `isScanning` is true (no promise to share). Two dispatches in quick succession, or a dispatch during project setup's first scan, compose the prompt (src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:236-245) with dynamicContext null or stale - no classes, plugins or build deps in the Project Context header. Fixed = projectStore keeps the in-flight scan promise and scanProject returns it (the pattern useModuleAggregates uses for its in-flight fetch), or execute waits for isScanning to clear with a bounded timeout.

## Flow
- project setup starts a scan (isScanning true)
- user clicks a checklist item
- execute: scanProject returns immediately -> composeTaskDispatch ctx.dynamicContext null -> prompt lacks project classes

## Expected impact
The first dispatches of a session carry the project context they were meant to. Could break: execute latency rises by up to one scan.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every dispatch carries the project scan
Before: awaited in-flight scans: 0 (projectStore.ts:120 early return)
After: predicted: test with isScanning true and a delayed scan -> composeTaskDispatch receives the scanned context
Method: simulation - the fix site is src/stores/projectStore.ts, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook(useModuleCLI) with projectStore isScanning=true and a scan that resolves after 50 ms; assert the ctx passed to composeTaskDispatch has dynamicContext

title: NBA deadline cache never sees a deadline saved in the Calendar Roadmap
body:
## Summary
useMilestoneDeadlines caches /api/milestone-deadlines for the process lifetime and the only writer (Calendar Roadmap) never invalidates it, so NBA ranks against the deadlines read at first mount.

## Description
src/hooks/useMilestoneDeadlines.ts:40 process-wide `cache`, :52-64 load only once, no exported invalidator. src/components/modules/evaluator/CalendarRoadmapView/useCalendarRoadmapView.ts:44-49 is a SECOND read path for the same endpoint (raw fetch) and :61-65 PUTs a deadline without telling the NBA cache. Same shape as the run-evidence gap fixed this round (f7fc3c1e). Fixed = export invalidateMilestoneDeadlines() from the hook, call it after the PUT, and move the roadmap's read onto the shared hook.

## Flow
- NBA card mounted (deadline cache filled)
- set a milestone due tomorrow in Calendar Roadmap
- NBA ranking unchanged until reload

## Expected impact
A deadline the user just set moves the next-best-action at once. Could break: nothing visible beyond one extra GET per save.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - NBA reads the current deadlines
Before: invalidators: 0; read paths for /api/milestone-deadlines: 2
After: predicted: 1 invalidator called by the writer; 1 read path
Method: simulation - the writer is in the evaluator context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: renderHook(useMilestoneDeadlines) + call the roadmap save; assert a second GET and the new deadline in result.deadlines

title: A cancelled spend preflight leaves the caller's step "running" forever
body:
## Summary
useModuleCLI.execute resolves void both when it dispatched and when the user cancelled the preflight, so callers that mark a step running before execute never learn nothing ran.

## Description
src/hooks/useModuleCLI.ts:221-224 `if (!proceed) return;` resolves the same Promise<void> as a dispatch. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_character/wizard/CharacterSourceWizard.tsx:103-107 marks step 2 running and executes TaskFactory.characterSetup (an EXPENSIVE type, src/lib/cli-spend/preflight.ts:23-31); on cancel no run starts, onComplete never fires and the step spins forever. Fixed = execute returns Promise<boolean> (true = dispatched); callers that set pending state revert it on false. In-tree contract widening; every current caller ignores the return value, so it is backward compatible.

## Flow
- budget near limit -> preflight dialog opens
- user clicks Cancel
- wizard step 2 stays running; no session exists to end it

## Expected impact
Cancel puts the step back to idle. Could break: none - a void-returning caller ignores the boolean.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a cancelled dispatch is visible to its caller
Before: execute outcomes distinguishable by the caller: 1 of 2 (dispatch vs cancel both void)
After: predicted: 2 of 2; wizard test with requestPreflightConfirm -> false asserts step idle
Method: simulation - the stuck state is in another context's component
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: hook test: mock fetchPreflightVerdict warn + requestPreflightConfirm false -> execute resolves false; CharacterSourceWizard test asserts step reverts

title: Retry on the NBA caches can be overwritten by the older in-flight read
body:
## Summary
useMilestoneDeadlines.retry and useModuleRunEvidence retry/invalidate drop the in-flight entry and start a new read, but the old read still writes the cache when it resolves, possibly after the new one.

## Description
src/hooks/useMilestoneDeadlines.ts:76-80 sets cache={} and calls load(); the earlier promise's `.then` (:56-59) still assigns `cache` unconditionally. src/hooks/useModuleRunEvidence.ts loadModule/loadProject `.then` writes (moduleCache.set / projectCache =) are likewise unguarded, which also applies to invalidateRunEvidence. The pair in this context has the guard: src/hooks/useModuleAggregates.ts:86-91 and :144-147 use a generation counter so a pre-invalidation load never seats itself. Fixed = the same generation guard in both caches.

## Flow
- read A in flight (slow)
- retry/invalidate starts read B
- B resolves (fresh), then A resolves and overwrites with the pre-write answer

## Expected impact
A refresh can never land an older answer over a newer one. Could break: nothing; only stale writes are dropped.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - newest read wins
Before: generation-guarded caches: 1 of 3 (aggregates only)
After: predicted: 3 of 3; test resolving A after B asserts B's data stays
Method: simulation - out-of-order resolution walked through the code; not built this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: deferred-promise test: start read A, retry (read B), resolve B then A; assert the cache holds B
